Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Credible secondary reference indicates Guinea‑Bissau has no data protection legislation (and no data protection authority appointed).
revision_notes: Verified via Data Protection Africa factsheet (confirms no data protection law and no appointed authority) and cross-checked against a Paradigm Initiative press release (29 January 2026) that lists Guinea-Bissau among the countries still lacking data protection legislation, plus a 2025 World Bank digital legal-framework assessment noting draft data protection and cybercrime laws remain unenacted. No evidence of payment-specific data provisions. Score of 1 (No) confirmed and unchanged.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau has no national data protection or privacy legislation and has not appointed a data protection authority. A draft data protection law has been developed but not enacted. There are consequently no legal provisions, general or payment-specific, governing the collection, storage, sharing, retention or use of payment transaction data.
